newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana stocks slip further in deserted bourse.
newsitem.headline: Ghana stocks slip further in deserted bourse.

text.p: Ghanaian shares extended their downward trend from last week, with big buyers remaining on the sidelines on Monday, dealers said.
The GSE All-Share Index dropped marginally by 0.16 points to close at 365.58 on lowly volume of 11,530 shares traded compared with 85,940 on Friday.
No stock gained, two declined and the rest were unchanged.

The bourse is weighed down by poor sentiment resulting from general economic worries. Some traders and experts fear it may be entering a pre-election correction after a series of bull sessions. Presidential and general elections are due on December 7.

Peter Addae of the Ghana Stock Exchange told Reuters: "Everybody seems a little cautious ahead of December elections and because of worries about interest rates, even though relevant indicators for the companies look positive."
There were trickles of individual investor selling without active demand, pushing the total number of shares offered to 1.2 million against demand of 168,000 shares.
"This is a supply-driven session," said a dealer, who expects the situation to persist for a while because of the absence of institutional buyers.
Ghana Commercial Bank, one of the stars of recent sessions, dropped a cedi to 718 cedis while trading group CFAO also fell one cedi to 19.
Market capitalisation eased to 2,862.65 billion cedis from 2,862.87 billion cedis.
